notWritten.reason: the descriptor exists and is unreachable. decideBinding consults protectCategoryOf BEFORE it matches any descriptor, and the protect vocabulary holds /\bconvict(ed|ion)\b/ under `disposition_or_hearing`. Measured in this worktree: protectCategoryOf("Conviction date") and protectCategoryOf("Date of conviction") both return disposition_or_hearing, and the form's own printed heading is DATE OF CONVICTION. matter.conviction_date, flagged requiresExplicitMapping so a caller must name it deliberately, is therefore reachable from no caption at all.
notWritten.whatThisLaneDidNotDo: word the binding label until the protect rule stops firing. That is the same move as wording a refusal until an approved-reason regex accepts it, and it would have put a court's determination on a sworn filing through a rule written to stop exactly that. The shared rule was not changed either: it governs forty-odd families under other lanes' claims.
notWritten.consequence: this family deliberately holds NO conviction_date in its charge rows, so that declaring the column participant-supplied is a true statement rather than a convenient one. The self-test asserts the absence in both fixtures.
notWritten.disposition: REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, declared on all four rows and disclosed, with the form's instruction 4 and the certified-copy attachment cited
notWritten.raisedFor: the shared registry owner, in build-findings.json under severity shared-registry: a descriptor no caption can reach proves nothing.

rowAtomicity.why: The fitter refuses a value the issuer's box cannot show, which is right one cell at a time and wrong one ROW at a time: the first render of the boundary record left rows a and c empty while b and d were filled, and no counter can see that - rowKeyOf reads a row number out of a field name or a printed label and this form numbers its lines a to d, so the table is never measured as rows.
rowAtomicity.how: the document is rendered twice. The first render is a measurement through the same fitter that will draw the cells; any conviction row with a refused cell then goes to the second render as unwritable-by-role, whole, and is declared and disclosed like a row the platform never held. The second render produces the bytes.
rowAtomicity.measuredHere: boundary row a repeats the caption's own 28-character case number, which needs 92.4pt in 92pt of usable column; the row is withheld whole and the delivered table lists three convictions.
rowAtomicity.enforced: the self-test asserts that no conviction row has one writable cell written and another declared.

whatTheFreshIndependentReadShouldRuleOn: Whether item 1 as delivered states the record correctly: the crime and case number in their own columns, the charge-code and date columns blank, and no row half-written. The row-atomicity rule is enforced in the builder and asserted in its self-test; it is not visible to any of the nine counters, so it needs eyes.

Whether writing item 2 at all is right on an application sworn under penalty of perjury. This lane's position is that the platform lays out the participant's own held words and composes none of them, that a statement it does not hold leaves all five lines blank, and that the instructions tell the filer in bold to read and correct item 2 before signing. That is a judgement a reviewer may take differently, and it is the single most consequential thing in this repair.

Whether the caption's multiple-case-numbers box should be settled by the build at all, and whether settling it from the DELIVERED table rather than from the held facts is the right rule. A withheld row is not a listed one, which is why it is decided after the measurement render.

Whether leaving the conviction-date column blank is right, given that the platform's schema has a slot for the fact and the shared protect vocabulary is what forbids writing it. The alternative was to word the binding label until the protect rule stopped firing; this lane refused to and raised the unreachable descriptor instead.

The two new shared-finalizer channels, narrativeAcrossFields and selectionsFromHeldFacts, and the composedFieldValues channel from the integrated pass. All three are opt-in and default to empty; three other families were rebuilt byte-identical under them.
